vectors.guidance_rule: A search_car_price call with an empty or whitespace-only brand_name must be denied for all roles.
vectors.reason: If brand_name is omitted entirely from args, args.brand_name is undefined; trim_space(undefined) does not equal "" in Rego, so the empty-brand deny rule never fires, and the restricted-brand deny rule also skips (trim_space check passes as non-empty is not evaluated), allowing a call with no brand_name.
vectors.exploit_strategy: Send a search_car_price request with no brand_name field in args (omit it entirely). The empty-check deny rule silently fails because args.brand_name is undefined, and the restricted-brand rule's trim_space guard also fails to trigger, so allow fires.

vectors.guidance_rule: vehicle_type is matched exactly and case-sensitively against these lowercase values. Any other value — including different casing — is denied for every role.
rules_involved: deny[msg] if { input.name == "get_vehicles_by_type"; subject.user_role in valid_roles; subject.user_role != "guest"; not args.vehicle_type in allowed_vehicle_types_by_role[subject.user_role] ... }
vectors.reason: vehicle_type is optional (default 'carros' in the tool schema). If omitted, args.vehicle_type is undefined. 'undefined in set' evaluates to false in Rego, so 'not ... in ...' is true and the deny fires — but only for roles whose allowed set does not include undefined. However, for analyst the set includes all types; undefined is still not in the set, so deny fires correctly. The real issue: the backend default coerces missing vehicle_type to 'carros', which the guidance says the policy must reject rather than rely on. For consumer/journalist the deny correctly fires on undefined, but for analyst undefined is also not in the set so deny fires too — this is actually correct. Re-examining: the divergence is that a fleet_manager omitting vehicle_type gets denied (correct), but the guidance says the policy must reject unrecognized types rather than rely on backend fallback — the policy does deny undefined, so this is fine. The actual omitted_field divergence is for brand_name as described above.
vectors.exploit_strategy: N/A — this specific sub-case is actually handled correctly by the policy.

vectors.guidance_rule: A search_car_price call with an empty or whitespace-only brand_name must be denied for all roles. brand_name compared by exact case-sensitive equality; partial or differently-cased names are denied.
rules_involved: deny[msg] if { input.name == "search_car_price"; subject.user_role in object.keys(allowed_brands_by_role); trim_space(args.brand_name) != ""; not args.brand_name in allowed_brands_by_role[subject.user_role] ... }
vectors.reason: When brand_name is omitted, args.brand_name is undefined. trim_space(undefined) is undefined, which is neither == "" nor != "", so both the empty-check deny and the restricted-brand deny silently fail. A fleet_manager or journalist can call search_car_price with no brand_name and the policy allows it.
vectors.exploit_strategy: As fleet_manager or journalist, send search_car_price with args={} (no brand_name key). Both deny rules referencing brand_name fail due to undefined, so allow=true.
